query: Before I present our checkout test tomorrow: a colleague ran a chi-square on the assignment counts (counts.csv, intended 50/50) and got p = 0.01, and now the team is saying the test has sample ratio mismatch and the whole thing is invalid. The primary result was +1.9pp on completion, CI [0.6, 3.2], full pre-registered horizon, exposure even across arms. Do we really have to throw the test away?
expected_behavior: Applies the SRM convention correctly: the check runs at alpha 0.001, not 0.05, precisely because it runs on every test and would otherwise cry wolf; p = 0.01 at these counts passes the gate, so the test is not invalidated and the +1.9pp result stands (worth noting the ratio is unusual and monitoring assignment on the next run, but not blocking). States the threshold and the reason for it rather than treating any p < 0.05 as a broken test. Without the skill, the model typically agrees that p = 0.01 indicates SRM and recommends distrusting or rerunning the test.
